purpose: Provenance metadata for reference-only cross-genre observations and original AnotherLife evaluation methods.

rightsPolicy.rule: URLs and concise observations are recorded for review. Linked publisher media remains third-party reference material and is not an AnotherLife asset.
rightsPolicy.approvalBoundary: No source row approves copying, production use, final balance, implementation, visual direction, monetization, or release.

sourceClasses.OfficialDeveloper: Publisher, developer, platform owner, or first-party support material.
sourceClasses.MaintainedCommunity: Maintained community documentation used to form tests, not a developer contract.
sourceClasses.CommunityReverseEngineering: Player-derived behavior or formula hypothesis requiring independent verification.
sourceClasses.ResearchStandard: Published research, statistical guidance, or an openly described ranking method.

linkAudit.method: Automated HEAD and GET checks followed by search-index and page-content inspection for blocked responses.
linkAudit.blockedStatus: Each listed URL returned HTTP 403 to the direct automated checker but remained indexed with matching publisher/community page identity and content. Treat them as automation-blocked, not dead.
linkAudit.notes: Three initial HEAD-only 404 responses were resolved by GET or corrected canonical URL: the Black Desert Node War page, Guild Wars 2 culling page, and Microsoft TrueSkill project page.

sources.pageTitle: Get Into the Grid of Things with the Updated UI and HUD
sources.observation: The publisher documents configurable HUD placement, grid alignment, saved layouts, and accessibility-oriented interaction options.
sources.applicability: Supports testing configurable hierarchy and saved profiles without copying layout or art.
sources.notes: Trademark and screenshots belong to their owner; URLs are reference-only.

sources.pageTitle: Get Ready for the Battleground Blitz Brawl
sources.observation: The rules make capture, respawn, lockout, and objective timing explicit.
sources.applicability: Motivates truthful objective state and timing tests.
sources.notes: Do not import branded terminology or exact rules.

sources.observation: The publisher describes bounded war participation, objectives, stages, and rule-specific stat treatment.
sources.applicability: Supports mode-separated profiles and explicit war-state communication.
sources.notes: Live rules can change; date and region must accompany any test.

sources.observation: The developer explains broad accuracy/evasion adjustments and separate combat contexts.
sources.applicability: Motivates explicit probability bounds and mode-versioned coefficients.
sources.notes: No published numeric formula is adopted.

sources.observation: The developer documents systemic hit-count, damage-calculation, and stat-behavior adjustments.
sources.applicability: Supports testing hit distributions, damage tails, and stat interactions.
sources.notes: Observation is qualitative; AnotherLife equations are independent.

sources.pageTitle: World vs. World: The End of Culling
sources.observation: The developer discusses representing many nearby players through staged model fallback rather than hiding actors.
sources.applicability: Supports fidelity-before-truth degradation and actor-count measurements.
sources.notes: Historical architecture evidence, not a current performance guarantee.

sources.observation: The maintained wiki inventories objective ownership, siege, supply, scoring, and map-state concepts.
sources.applicability: Forms scenario categories for map-front comprehension; it is not an AnotherLife rule source.
sources.notes: Community-maintained and patch-sensitive.

sources.pageTitle: Community Update: Vengeance Testing in Cyrodiil
sources.observation: Official forum updates describe testing a reduced-complexity combat profile to support larger Cyrodiil populations and performance study.
sources.applicability: Motivates joint client/server/network/effect evaluation rather than renderer-only optimization.
sources.notes: Test results do not establish AnotherLife capacity.

sources.observation: The publisher explains siege objectives and visual allegiance/leader markers for large group conflict.
sources.applicability: Supports testing color-independent allegiance and objective hierarchy.
sources.notes: Linked images remain publisher-owned reference media.

sources.topic: all, guild, party, and self VFX filtering
sources.observation: Patch notes document settings that distinguish effect sources and reduce large-combat visual load.
sources.applicability: Supports independently configurable effect-source categories; it does not evidence target or nameplate filtering.
sources.notes: Settings and names are not copied.

sources.pageTitle: Dev Talk: Faction Objectives and Provinces
sources.observation: The developer describes attack direction, province control, fortification, and transport relationships.
sources.applicability: Motivates a measurable front-discovery and travel-to-contribution journey.
sources.notes: Do not import map structure or terminology.

sources.pageTitle: A Brief Guide to Zerg Mechanics
sources.observation: The developer provides a conceptual guide to large-group pressure controls.
sources.applicability: Motivates bounded, explainable pressure tests rather than one hidden comeback scalar.
sources.notes: AnotherLife formulas in the companion document are independently authored.

sources.observation: The developer discusses effect and character presentation changes for large battles.
sources.applicability: Supports actor/effect-tier profiling and protected gameplay cues.
sources.notes: Historical evidence; no capacity claim.

sources.observation: The publisher describes route, visibility, collision, lighting, and vegetation adjustments to a competitive map.
sources.applicability: Supports route-time and visibility budgets under each lighting/weather state.
sources.notes: Linked map image remains publisher-owned.

sources.observation: The publisher describes staged capture objectives, fort assault, and siege equipment.
sources.applicability: Motivates explicit objective progression and contributor roles.
sources.notes: Linked image remains publisher-owned.

sources.topic: realm identity and durable player-driven war
sources.observation: The developer-provided listing describes realm choice and large-scale, player-driven Realm-versus-Realm and PvP as the product's central identity.
sources.applicability: Preserves the existing AnotherLife benchmark focus on realm identity and long-term group-war purpose.
sources.notes: No realm names, races, classes, maps, rules, rewards, art, or terminology are adopted.

sources.pageTitle: AION 2 Introduces Major Class Overhaul and Unveils Chaotic Abyss
sources.observation: Developer material documents separated PvP/PvE damage calculations and a limit on consecutively applied immune or immortal effects.
sources.applicability: Motivates separate mode coefficients, impact readability, and immunity-chain telemetry.
sources.notes: Aspirational visual reference only; linked image remains publisher-owned.

sources.topic: arena, battlefield, rift, and large-force conflict
sources.pageTitle: AION 2 Showcases Core Combat Content and Signature Dungeon Gameplay
sources.observation: Developer material identifies Arena, Battlefield, Rift, and Abyss as competitive PvP modes.
sources.applicability: Supports testing separate profiles by mode rather than extrapolating one combat environment.
sources.notes: No mode, name, population, or rule is adopted.

sources.observation: The official store listing presents city restoration, development, composition, and alliance conflict as connected loops.
sources.applicability: Supports visible construction consequence and composition-readiness tests.
sources.notes: Store claims require runtime verification before use as detailed behavior evidence.

sources.observation: Official material describes territory, assistance, research, rallies, and shared alliance benefits.
sources.applicability: Motivates legible shared benefits and rally-state requirements.
sources.notes: No exact alliance economy is adopted.

sources.topic: building, research, troops, formations, guilds, and rallies
sources.pageTitle: Lords Mobile: Kingdom Wars on Google Play
sources.observation: The official listing presents a compact multi-system kingdom and guild-war loop.
sources.applicability: Supports command-loop and counter/readiness comprehension tests.
sources.notes: Monetization patterns are explicitly outside the approved benchmark outcome.

sources.pageTitle: Clash of Clans on Google Play
sources.observation: The official listing presents building, upgrading, attacking, friendly competition, and replay-oriented learning.
sources.applicability: Motivates teaching one loop and enabling risk-free rehearsal.
sources.notes: No base layout, troop, art, or UI is adopted.

sources.pageTitle: The State of Gameplay and What's Ahead
sources.observation: The developer discusses balance health using more than aggregate success, including composition concentration and player experience.
sources.applicability: Supports role/composition diversity analysis alongside outcome metrics.
sources.notes: No comparator tuning is imported.

sources.observation: Official material presents a shared construction contribution loop.
sources.applicability: Motivates meaningful small contributions with clear shared-state projection.
sources.notes: No economy or progression value is adopted.

sources.topic: troop control, gates, terrain, weather, and scale
sources.publisherOrMaintainer: World's Edge and TiMi Studio Group
sources.observation: Official product material emphasizes troop control, siege targets, terrain, weather, alliances, and large battlefields.
sources.applicability: Supports route, gate, siege, selection, and scale-readability test categories.
sources.notes: Franchise names, units, art, and exact interactions are not adopted.

sources.pageTitle: Age of Empires Mobile on Google Play
sources.observation: The official listing connects city development, commanders, alliances, and real-time field control.
sources.applicability: Motivates coherent city-to-war state and mobile command readability.
sources.notes: Store claims are not performance or player-acceptance evidence.

sources.topic: zoom context, terrain, passes, and moving orders
sources.pageTitle: Rise of Kingdoms: Lost Crusade on Google Play
sources.observation: The official listing presents continuous map zoom, terrain/pass strategy, and armies that can receive orders while moving.
sources.applicability: Supports progressive disclosure and explicit replace/queue/cancel march semantics.
sources.notes: No map, civilization, commander, or command UI is adopted.

sources.topic: own squad, preparation, reward, and map labels
sources.observation: Official update material calls out rally preparation, own-squad information, reward previews, labels, recommendations, and contextual messages.
sources.applicability: Supports a self-locating, truthful rally information contract.
sources.notes: No reward or alliance algorithm is adopted.

sources.observation: The official page presents scouting and planning before attacking.
sources.applicability: Motivates preview or simulation before irreversible loss.
sources.notes: No island, base, troop, or art treatment is adopted.

sources.observation: Official notes discuss improvements for returning players and account access around onboarding.
sources.applicability: Supports recovery/login before forcing onboarding replay.
sources.notes: Exact product flow must be rechecked if used in a future dated audit.

sources.observation: Platform guidance explains frame pacing and selecting sustainable presentation rates.
sources.applicability: Supports measuring frame-time distributions and deliberate 30/60 FPS tiers.
sources.notes: Supported devices and pass targets still require project approval.

sources.observation: Platform guidance covers game interaction and readable interfaces across supported input contexts.
sources.applicability: Forms platform-specific accessibility and device test categories.
sources.notes: Guidance does not replace testing on AnotherLife target devices.

sources.observation: The community documents a patch-sensitive model of damage components.
sources.applicability: Useful only for identifying variables and regression questions; no formula is copied.
sources.notes: Reverse-engineered/community-derived behavior requires independent verification.

sources.observation: The maintained wiki describes converting control effects into break-bar pressure.
sources.applicability: Motivates boss break-bar test categories; AnotherLife's model is original.
sources.notes: Not a developer contract and not copied tuning.

sources.observation: The maintained wiki describes a patch-sensitive mechanic relating affected targets to area-effect pressure.
sources.applicability: Motivates clump and target-cap scenarios; no coefficients or formula are copied.
sources.notes: Community reference only.

sources.observation: The maintained wiki records a patch-sensitive large-group pressure mechanic.
sources.applicability: Motivates population boundary and abuse tests; AnotherLife equations are independently authored.
sources.notes: Community-maintained reference only; direct automated access was blocked with HTTP 403 during this audit.

sources.observation: The maintained wiki records a patch-sensitive protection concept based on the number of attackers affecting a target.
sources.applicability: Motivates attacker-count, attribution, timing-window, and abuse tests; AnotherLife equations are independently authored.
sources.notes: Community-maintained reference only; direct automated access was blocked with HTTP 403 during this audit.

sources.observation: Published research describes a Bayesian skill-rating approach with uncertainty.
sources.applicability: Supports comparing calibration and uncertainty handling; it does not select an AnotherLife algorithm.
sources.notes: Implementation and licensing require separate review if selected.

sources.pageTitle: TrueSkill 2: An improved Bayesian skill rating system
sources.observation: Published research explores a Bayesian rating model with additional performance observations.
sources.applicability: Supports evaluation questions about calibration and data minimization.
sources.notes: Do not ingest behavioral features without privacy and fairness review.

sources.observation: The published specification defines rating, uncertainty, and volatility concepts.
sources.applicability: Provides an alternate calibration benchmark; no system selection is approved.
sources.notes: Any implementation requires separate technical and rights review.

sources.pageTitle: Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in A/B Testing
sources.observation: Research guidance explains why assignment/exposure mismatch can invalidate an experiment.
sources.applicability: Requires an SRM check before interpreting balance experiments.
sources.notes: Statistical passage never replaces human gates.

sources.publisherOrMaintainer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.observation: The handbook presents methods for uncertainty around binomial proportions.
sources.applicability: Supports reporting uncertainty for rates instead of point estimates alone.
sources.notes: Choose the interval based on the analysis design.

sources.pageTitle: Always Valid Inference: Bringing Sequential Analysis to A/B Testing
sources.observation: The paper discusses inference designed for sequential monitoring.
sources.applicability: Motivates predeclared stopping rules or suitable sequential methods.
sources.notes: Method choice requires statistical review.

sources.pageTitle: On video game balancing: Joining player and data-driven analytics
sources.observation: The research frames game balancing as a combination of player-centered and data-driven evidence.
sources.applicability: Supports retaining qualitative playtest and comprehension evidence alongside telemetry.
sources.notes: No study text or proprietary instrument is copied.
